title: Frontend Development
tagline: Interfaces built for speed, accessibility and pixel-perfect polish.
overview: We build the layer your users actually touch — fast-loading, accessible interfaces that hold up across devices and don't regress every time a new feature ships. Component-driven architecture means your design system stays consistent as the product grows.

use_cases.title: Marketing sites that load instantly
use_cases.desc: Static generation and image optimization tuned so Core Web Vitals pass on real connections, not just lab tests.

use_cases.title: SaaS dashboards at scale
use_cases.desc: Component libraries and state management that stay maintainable as a dashboard grows past a dozen views.

use_cases.title: Design systems your team can extend
use_cases.desc: Token-based theming and documented components so new features stay visually consistent without a designer re-reviewing every screen.

process.title: Component Audit
process.desc: We review existing UI (or design files) to define a shared component vocabulary before building anything.

process.title: Build the System
process.desc: Core components and design tokens are built first, so every screen after this reuses the same building blocks.

process.title: Assemble Screens
process.desc: Full pages and flows are assembled from the component system, reviewed against real device performance.

process.title: Test & Harden
process.desc: Cross-browser, accessibility and performance testing before anything ships to production.

faqs.q: Do you work with our existing design system or build a new one?
faqs.a: Both — we extend an existing system where one exists, or build one from scratch if your product doesn't have one yet.

faqs.q: How do you handle browser and device compatibility?
faqs.a: Every build is tested against a defined support matrix (browsers, OS versions, screen sizes) agreed with you before development starts.

faqs.q: Can your frontend team work alongside our in-house backend developers?
faqs.a: Yes, we regularly integrate with existing backend teams via API contracts agreed upfront.

testimonial.quote: Our dashboard went from feeling sluggish to loading instantly, and our internal team can now add new views without breaking the layout.
testimonial.author: Client Name

title: Backend Development
tagline: The systems underneath that keep running when nobody's watching.
overview: Reliable, well-documented backend systems — APIs, business logic and data processing — built to handle real production load, not just pass a demo. We favor boring, provable architecture over clever code that's hard to hand off.

use_cases.title: REST and GraphQL APIs
use_cases.desc: Documented, versioned APIs designed for the clients that will actually consume them — web, mobile or third parties.

use_cases.title: Microservices done deliberately
use_cases.desc: We only split services where it solves a real scaling or team problem, not by default, to avoid unnecessary operational overhead.

use_cases.title: Payment and billing systems
use_cases.desc: Idempotent, auditable payment flows built with reconciliation and failure handling in mind from day one.

process.title: Requirements & Data Modeling
process.desc: We map the domain and data model before choosing a framework or writing any endpoints.

process.title: API Contract First
process.desc: Endpoints are specified and agreed with frontend/mobile teams before backend implementation begins.

process.title: Build & Test
process.desc: Automated tests cover business logic, not just happy paths, before code reaches staging.

process.title: Load Test & Harden
process.desc: Realistic load testing and monitoring setup before anything handles production traffic.

faqs.q: Which backend language or framework do you recommend?
faqs.a: It depends on your team's existing stack and hiring plans — we'll recommend the option that's easiest for your team to maintain long term, not just what's fastest for us to build.

faqs.q: How do you handle API documentation?
faqs.a: Every API ships with OpenAPI/Swagger documentation kept in sync with the actual implementation.

faqs.q: Can you take over an existing backend codebase?
faqs.a: Yes, we start with a codebase and architecture audit before making changes to an existing system.

testimonial.quote: They inherited a backend nobody wanted to touch and had it stable and documented within a month.
testimonial.author: Client Name

title: Mobile Technologies
tagline: Apps that feel native, whether they're built native or not.
overview: iOS, Android and cross-platform mobile development for products where performance and offline reliability actually matter — not just apps that work fine on a fast connection in a demo.

use_cases.title: Consumer apps built for retention
use_cases.desc: Onboarding, push notifications and performance tuned around the metrics that actually predict retention.

use_cases.title: Field service apps that work offline
use_cases.desc: Offline-first data sync for teams working in warehouses, job sites or areas with unreliable connectivity.

use_cases.title: On-demand marketplaces
use_cases.desc: Real-time location, matching and payment flows built to handle two-sided marketplace traffic patterns.

process.title: Platform Strategy
process.desc: We assess whether native, Flutter or React Native fits your performance needs and budget before committing.

process.title: Prototype & Validate
process.desc: A clickable prototype tests the core flow with real users before full development starts.

process.title: Build on Real Devices
process.desc: Development and testing happen on physical devices throughout, not just simulators.

process.title: Store Launch & Iterate
process.desc: App store submission handled for you, with a plan for the first post-launch update cycle.

faqs.q: Should we go native or cross-platform?
faqs.a: For most products, Flutter or React Native gets you to market faster at lower cost. We recommend native only when performance or platform-specific APIs demand it.

faqs.q: How do you handle offline functionality?
faqs.a: Local data storage with conflict-resolution sync logic, so the app stays usable without a connection and reconciles cleanly once it's back.

faqs.q: Do you support both iOS and Android from one codebase?
faqs.a: Yes, with Flutter or React Native we typically maintain a single codebase for both platforms, with native modules where needed.

testimonial.quote: Our field technicians can now log jobs with zero signal and everything syncs perfectly once they're back in range.
testimonial.author: Client Name

title: Cloud & DevOps
tagline: Infrastructure that scales quietly and recovers on its own.
overview: Cloud architecture, CI/CD pipelines and infrastructure automation designed so deployments are routine events, not incidents. We build for the traffic and team size you're growing into, not just what you need today.

use_cases.title: Cloud migrations without downtime
use_cases.desc: Phased migration plans with rollback points, so moving to the cloud doesn't mean a weekend of crossed fingers.

use_cases.title: CI/CD pipelines that catch problems early
use_cases.desc: Automated testing and deployment gates so bad code doesn't reach production because a human forgot a step.

use_cases.title: Auto-scaling for unpredictable traffic
use_cases.desc: Infrastructure that scales up for a traffic spike and back down afterward, without a 2 a.m. phone call.

process.title: Infrastructure Audit
process.desc: We review your current setup, costs and failure points before proposing any changes.

process.title: Architecture Design
process.desc: A target architecture is documented and reviewed with your team before migration begins.

process.title: Automate & Migrate
process.desc: Infrastructure-as-code and CI/CD pipelines are built alongside a phased, low-risk migration.

process.title: Monitor & Optimize
process.desc: Ongoing monitoring and cost optimization once the new infrastructure is live.

faqs.q: Which cloud provider do you recommend?
faqs.a: Usually whichever your team already has experience with — AWS, Azure and GCP all fit most use cases. We'll flag it if a specific requirement points toward one.

faqs.q: How do you avoid downtime during a migration?
faqs.a: Migrations run in phases with defined rollback points, and traffic is cut over gradually rather than all at once.

faqs.q: Do you manage infrastructure after the migration is done?
faqs.a: Yes, most clients move onto a managed infrastructure plan with monitoring, patching and cost reviews.

testimonial.quote: We migrated to AWS with zero customer-facing downtime, which our last provider told us was impossible.
testimonial.author: Client Name

title: Database Solutions
tagline: Data architecture that stays fast as it grows, not just on day one.
overview: Schema design, query optimization and data migration for systems where data integrity and query speed actually matter at scale — from relational systems to the caching and search layers around them.

use_cases.title: Data warehousing for reporting
use_cases.desc: Structured warehouses that keep reporting queries fast without slowing down your production database.

use_cases.title: Real-time analytics pipelines
use_cases.desc: Event streaming and caching layers so dashboards reflect activity within seconds, not overnight batch jobs.

use_cases.title: Multi-tenant architecture
use_cases.desc: Data isolation strategies that keep tenants secure without duplicating infrastructure per customer.

process.title: Data Audit
process.desc: We review your current schema, query patterns and pain points before recommending changes.

process.title: Schema Design
process.desc: A normalized (or deliberately denormalized) schema designed around your actual access patterns.

process.title: Migrate & Index
process.desc: Data migration with integrity checks, plus indexing strategy tuned to your slowest real queries.

process.title: Monitor & Tune
process.desc: Ongoing query performance monitoring and tuning as data volume grows.

faqs.q: Can you migrate data from a legacy database without downtime?
faqs.a: In most cases yes, using a phased dual-write or replication approach so the cutover is a non-event.

faqs.q: SQL or NoSQL — how do you decide?
faqs.a: It comes down to your data relationships and query patterns. We recommend based on your actual use case, not a default preference.

faqs.q: How do you improve slow queries on an existing database?
faqs.a: We start by profiling your actual slow queries in production, not guessing — then index, restructure or cache based on real evidence.

testimonial.quote: A query that used to take 8 seconds now returns in under 100 milliseconds. Our support team stopped getting complaints about the dashboard overnight.
testimonial.author: Client Name

title: AI & Automation
tagline: Practical automation that removes real busywork, not a chatbot gimmick.
overview: We build automation and applied AI features that solve a specific, measurable problem — document processing, support triage, predictive alerts — rather than bolting AI onto a product because it's trending.

use_cases.title: Support ticket triage and drafting
use_cases.desc: Automatic categorization and draft responses that a human reviews and sends, cutting first-response time significantly.

use_cases.title: Predictive alerts from operational data
use_cases.desc: Models trained on your historical data to flag anomalies before they become incidents, not after.

use_cases.title: Document processing at scale
use_cases.desc: Extracting structured data from invoices, contracts or forms that used to require manual entry.

process.title: Problem Definition
process.desc: We define the specific, measurable outcome an automation or model needs to improve before building anything.

process.title: Data Assessment
process.desc: We review what data actually exists and whether it's sufficient before promising a model will work.

process.title: Build & Validate
process.desc: Models and workflows are tested against real historical cases, with accuracy reported honestly.

process.title: Deploy with Human Oversight
process.desc: Automation ships with a human-in-the-loop review step until accuracy is proven in production.

faqs.q: Do you build custom AI models or use existing APIs?
faqs.a: Most projects use existing models (like OpenAI's) fine-tuned or prompted for your use case — custom model training is reserved for cases where it's genuinely justified by the data and budget.

faqs.q: How do you handle AI accuracy and mistakes?
faqs.a: We report accuracy honestly based on testing, and typically recommend a human-review step until a workflow has proven reliable in production.

faqs.q: Is our data used to train external models?
faqs.a: No — we configure integrations to prevent your data being used for third-party model training unless you explicitly want that.

testimonial.quote: Our support team's first-response time dropped by half, and it only suggests drafts — a person still hits send.
testimonial.author: Client Name
testimonial.role: Head of Customer Support, Partner Company

title: API & Integration
tagline: Connecting the systems you already have, without duct tape.
overview: We connect your existing tools, payment providers and partner systems through well-documented, monitored integrations — so data flows automatically instead of living in someone's manual export-and-upload routine.

use_cases.title: Third-party tool integrations
use_cases.desc: Connecting your CRM, support desk and billing system so data updates in one place instead of three.

use_cases.title: Payment gateway integration
use_cases.desc: Stripe, PayPal or regional payment provider integrations built with reconciliation and failure handling in mind.

use_cases.title: Legacy system bridging
use_cases.desc: Middleware that lets a modern application talk to an older internal system without replacing it outright.

process.title: System Mapping
process.desc: We document what each system exposes and what data actually needs to flow between them.

process.title: Contract Design
process.desc: API contracts and authentication approach agreed upfront, including how failures are handled.

process.title: Build & Monitor
process.desc: Integrations are built with logging and alerting so failures are caught immediately, not discovered a week later.

process.title: Test Failure Paths
process.desc: We deliberately test what happens when an integration partner is slow or down, not just the happy path.

faqs.q: What happens if a third-party API goes down?
faqs.a: Integrations are built with retry logic, alerting and graceful degradation so a partner outage doesn't take down your whole system.

faqs.q: Can you design an API for our partners to integrate with?
faqs.a: Yes, we design and document partner-facing APIs, including versioning strategy and onboarding documentation.

faqs.q: Do you handle authentication and security for integrations?
faqs.a: Yes, OAuth 2.0 and API key management are handled as part of every integration, with credentials never hardcoded.

testimonial.quote: Data that used to be manually re-entered between our CRM and billing system now syncs automatically within seconds.
testimonial.author: Client Name
